summary: Template deployment atomicity failure caused partial macro publish and delayed SLA reporting
description: During a scheduled bulk publish of macros/templates to the new template indexer, the deployment job failed partway through and left an inconsistent state: some template versions were visible to the routing engine while others reverted to the old canonical index. The inconsistency caused a subset of internal tickets to be routed using stale SLA macros and produced gaps in the weekly SLA aggregation reports. Impact lasted ~3 hours until a manual reconciliation completed.
steps_to_reproduce: Run the template-publish job against a mixed-version batch while indexer migration flag is enabled (migration_v2=true).
Interrupt the job mid-run by simulating an indexer shard restart (kill process or rotate container).
Observe that template-service reports successful publish for subset of templates while indexer shows missing entries for others.
Trigger routing evaluation for affected queues and inspect which macro version was applied.
logs: 2026-03-10T09:15:01Z indexer ERROR shard-3 failed to commit: EOF
2026-03-10T11:58:12Z reconciliation INFO reindex-batch completed applied=265 missing=0 duration=2h43m
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: job-level commit is not transactional across old-index and new-index write paths when indexer migration flag is set.
Confirmed via logs that template-service returned success for individual writes, but indexer shard commit failed and publisher did not rollback successfully.
Routing-engine queried templates with mixed responses: some templates resolved to new-index IDs while others fell back to cached entries from the legacy indexer.
Reporting pipeline aggregates (daily_sla_cohorts) ingested partial template mappings during 09:12-12:00 UTC window, causing under-counts in P0/P1 escalations for specific queues.
mitigation: Paused all template-publish jobs immediately at 09:18 UTC across prod regions.
Ran reconciliation script (tools/template-reconciler v0.3) to re-publish missing template versions and force a single-source-of-truth refresh for template-service caches.
Replayed routing lookups for affected tickets to re-evaluate SLA assignment where safe; flagged tickets that had already been actioned to avoid duplication.
Backfilled reporting pipeline by reprocessing staging export for the 09:00-12:00 UTC window and re-running aggregation jobs.
Enabled stricter preflight checks on publisher to verify commit across both index paths before returning success (temporary guard added).
resolution: Root cause was a non-atomic publish path introduced during the indexer migration: publisher returned per-template write success without verifying commit across indexer shards, leaving a partial publish state when a shard failed. Fix applied: publisher now performs a two-phase commit with coordinator verification; reconciliation and reindex backfill completed on 2026-03-10 and reporting backfill finished by 2026-03-12. Issue marked Resolved after verification and monitoring for 48h.
